transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-09-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Redwood (Daniel, Maya, Lucas), Cygnus MedTech (Elena, Tom, Priya, Samir, Alicia)

[00:00] Daniel Park: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'll kick off real quick, hey elena, tom, thanks for making time. we wanted to run through our security posture and specifically the data treatment commitments you flagged in the intake form.
[00:18] Elena García: thanks daniel. we have a tight timeline — we need internal signoff from legal & security before the board meeting on 2028-10-05. primarily concerned about phasing and guarantee that no customer data will be used to train models. also auditability for compliance.
[00:33] Maya Singh: absolutely. i'll start with a high-level: redwood provides SOC 2 type II and we have ISO 27001 alignment workstreams; i'll go into specifics — but importantly we support customer managed keys and private deployments for data residency.
[00:48] Tom Reed: quick Q — SOC 2 report, recent, and is pen test available? also how granular are the audit logs? we need ability to tie a request id back to token-level metadata for forensics.
[01:05] Lucas Chen: yes we maintain request-level audit logs with timestamps, model variant, route, and redaction flag. retention window is configurable; default is 90 days in hosted. for Dedicated/Private you can request longer retention or export to your SIEM.
[01:27] Priya Nair: and for legal we need an explicit contract clause — no training on customer data, i.e., customer payloads won't be used to improve models. is that standard?
[01:39] Maya Singh: we can commit to a no-train/no-derive clause. hosted API has an opt-out and we can include it in the DPA. for Private deployments where the control plane is customer managed, there's no training at all by our service. we should note the difference: hosted can be configured not to train, Dedicated is isolated, Private is fully customer-controlled.
[02:03] Alicia Soto: what about ephemeral prompts — are prompts logged in full or partially redacted? we send PHI in some flows.
[02:12] Daniel Park: great point. by default, logs may include prompt text for debugging, but you can enable prompt-ephemerality mode where prompts are redacted at ingestion and only non-identifying metadata retained. that is an enterprise feature; we will include options in the pilot.
[02:31] Samir Patel: technical question — for customer-managed keys, do you integrate with our HSM in azure-key-vault / gcp-kms? does key material ever leave our KMS?
[02:43] Lucas Chen: we integrate with major KMS providers (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) via envelope encryption; key material never leaves the customer's KMS — Redwoods's runtime holds only wrapped keys. for on-prem HSM we can support a bring-your-own-HSM workflow using PKCS#11 connectors.
[03:01] Tom Reed: ok that helps. how about audit logs encryption and signing — we need non-repudiation for forward chain in case of incident.
[03:11] Maya Singh: logs are encrypted at rest and we can enable HMAC-signed append-only audit streams for Dedicated/Private. for hosted we provide signed digest exports on request and integrations to push to your SIEM in near-real-time.
[03:29] Elena García: can you map that to our compliance matrix — e.g., SOC 2 CC6, CC7 types? we need to demonstrate access control and monitoring.
[03:40] Daniel Park: yes — we have a controls matrix. maya can attach the SOC 2 mapping to your template.
[03:46] Maya Singh: noted, i'll include the mapping.
[03:50] Priya Nair: data residency — we have EU-only rule for production PHI; can you guarantee EU data centers only?
[03:59] Lucas Chen: yes we support region pinning. for hosted we can pin processing and storage to eu-west-region nodes. for additional assurance we recommend Private deployment inside your VPC in eu-west where logs and data never leave your network.
[04:17] Tom Reed: latency vs cost concern — if we use private deployment in our VPC, what changes in operational model and SLA?
[04:26] Daniel Park: Dedicated/Private increases cost but gives you full control and better isolation. SLAs are contractual — dedicated pools get latency SLOs and higher uptime guarantees. i'll send a short doc comparing latency and unit economics.
[04:40] Alicia Soto: regarding the 'no train' clause, what evidence can you provide to satisfy auditors? is there an end-to-end proof statement or logs showing training pipelines don't accept customer payloads?
[04:52] Maya Singh: we provide a DPA addendum plus a technical attestation: pipeline diagrams, config flags that disable data ingestion for internal training, and example audit entries that show training jobs use only curated open datasets. for higher assurance we can schedule a compliance workshop with our security engineering lead.
[05:12] Samir Patel: will you redact or pseudonymize PHI automatically? we need to ensure downstream logs and traces do not leak identifiers.
[05:22] Lucas Chen: we have an optional preprocessing hook — you can send data through our redaction service or run a client-side redaction library before sending. we also support post-ingest redaction and automatic tokenization/pseudonymization for known patterns. we'll test with your sample payloads.
[05:42] Tom Reed: what about retention controls? need enforcement so no one can change retention policy ad-hoc.
[05:49] Maya Singh: retention policies are role-gated and auditable via RBAC. only users with specific admin privileges can change retention; changes generate audit events and require approval workflow integration if you opt in.
[06:05] Elena García: SSO and RBAC — can we map our IdP groups to Redwood roles? we want least-privilege, separation of duties.
[06:14] Daniel Park: yes, SAML2.0 and OIDC supported. you can map IdP groups to RBAC roles (viewer, operator, admin, security-auditor). we also offer SCIM for provisioning.
[06:28] Priya Nair: logs of who accessed what — are those available for eDiscovery?
[06:34] Lucas Chen: yes access logs include user id (from SSO), action, resource, timestamp, and request id. can export in csv or stream into your log lake.
[06:44] Alicia Soto: curious about deletion semantics — if we delete a conversation, is it irrecoverable? for legal we need delete propagation guarantees within 24 hours.
[06:54] Maya Singh: deletions are soft-delete first — we keep tombstones for 24-72 hours to support in-flight operations; if you opt into strict deletion policy we can configure immediate cryptographic erasure where keys are rotated to render data unrecoverable within your retention SLA. that's typically part of the Private deployment contract.
[07:15] Tom Reed: helps. can we get an example of the audit log format? json sample?
[07:22] Daniel Park: yes we'll attach a sample. lucas to action.
[07:25] Samir Patel: one more — data in memory during inference: will tokens be persisted in any disk swap? we run in high-reg compliance environments.
[07:35] Lucas Chen: runtime keeps KV cache in memory; for Dedicated we avoid swapping to disk and disable swap by default. for hosted we employ encrypted swap and strict isolation; but if you need zero-disk persistence we recommend Private deployment.
[07:52] Elena García: what's the fallback / incident response process if there's a suspected leak?
[07:58] Maya Singh: we have an incident response plan with 24/7 on-call, runbooks for containment, and a communication template. breach notifications align with contract terms and regional laws. we can provide an example IR plan.
[08:12] Priya Nair: our legal team will want contractual indemnities and SLA credits. are you flexible?
[08:19] Daniel Park: we'll surface the options; some items are standard, some negotiable for enterprise customers. we'll have legal follow-up after the DPA draft.
[08:29] Alicia Soto: timeline recap — we need SOC2 report, DPA draft, pilot plan in eu region, and an initial redaction test with our sample PHI. can you confirm dates?
[08:43] Maya Singh: SOC2 + pen test by 2028-09-16; DPA draft by 2028-09-18; pilot week availability 2028-10-02 — we'll confirm exact windows after pricing signoff.
[08:58] Tom Reed: competitor question — you mentioned bigcloudai had less robust audit logs in our previous POC; can you summarize how redwood differs?
[09:08] Daniel Park: short answer: deeper audit fidelity, customer KMS, and private deployment options. BigCloudAI had hosted-only and fewer options for key control. VaultServe had good KMS but lacked model variant rollbacks and traceability at token level.
[09:26] Samir Patel: on the technical attestation, will you show configuration flags that disable learning pipelines?
[09:31] Maya Singh: yes we'll export the config flags and a short video showing the admin console where training flags are disabled for your tenant.
[09:39] Elena García: ok i'm satisfied this covers our checklist. a few small asks: ensure legal gets the DPA with explicit no-train language, ensure logs sample shows pseudonymization, and provide a clear on-prem runbook.
[09:53] Daniel Park: understood. we'll attach action items. thanks for the clear asks.
[09:59] Priya Nair: last question — if we go live, can you commit to quarterly compliance reviews and SOC reporting updates?
[10:07] Maya Singh: yes enterprise customers get quarterly reviews and we can align reporting cadence.
[10:13] Daniel Park: great — let's recap next steps.

Meeting recap / next steps (end of call):
- Redwood to share: SOC2 Type II report, pen test summary, SOC2 controls mapping, SAML/SCIM setup guide, sample audit log json, DPA draft with no-train clause, and pricing for Dedicated/Private.
- Cygnus to share: example PHI payloads for redaction testing, list of legal requirements.
- Schedule pilot for EU private deployment: target week 2028-10-02.

[END]
